message.reasoning:
I need to write JUnit 4 tests for the NodeUtil class from Closure-86b with high branch coverage, constructing real Node objects using com.google.javascript.rhino.Node and Token constants, along with TernaryValue since this comes from the actual Closure Compiler codebase.

Since Node is a rhino class without a mocking framework available (no Mockito in the classpath), I'll build Node trees directly using constructors like `new Node(Token.STRING, ...)`, `Node.newString(...)`, and `Node.newNumber(...)`. I'm planning to focus my tests on methods that are easy to verify without heavy AbstractCompiler dependency—things like getBooleanValue, getStringValue, getNumberValue, isImmutableValue, isLiteralValue, precedence, associativity/commutativity checks, assignment operator helpers, node type predicates (isGet, isName, isVar, etc.), loop and control structure helpers, and statement/block classification methods.

This continues into a broader sweep covering function-related checks (isFunction, isFunctionDeclaration, isVarArgsFunction, object call detection), prototype property helpers, node traversal utilities (visitPreOrder/visitPostOrder), try/catch/finally inspection, and various naming/reference counting utilities like getNameReferenceCount and getSourceName—giving me a solid map of which Node methods I can exercise directly with hand-built trees.

I'm now working through side-effect analysis methods like mayHaveSideEffects and functionCallHasSideEffects, which need an AbstractCompiler that can be null, plus canBeSideEffected and newFunctionNode. For newQualifiedNameNode, I'm weighing whether to skip it since it requires a CodingConvention implementation I'm not confident matches this old defects4j API version, though I could try writing a minimal anonymous implementation of the interface if needed.

Given the risk of importing unfamiliar classes, I'm deciding to keep tests scoped to Node, Token, TernaryValue, NodeUtil, and Rhino, passing null where AbstractCompiler is required, and building proper FUNCTION node trees (name, params, block) for tests like getFunctionName. I'll focus on well-understood methods and skip the trickier ones where behavior is uncertain.

Still checking the Node API methods...

There's also getParent, getAncestors, prop-based getters/setters, JSDoc access, and side-effect/qualified-name checks. I'm assuming addChildToBack sets the parent pointer automatically, but given how uncertain I am about the exact API surface for this spec version, I should be careful not to over-rely on assumptions here.

Still verifying available methods...

For the `var x = 5;` case, I'm confirming the pattern: create a NUMBER node for the value, attach it as a child of a NAME node, then wrap that NAME node inside a VAR node -- so the parent chain runs VAR → NAME → NUMBER.

For assignment expressions like `x = 5;`, the ASSIGN node's first child is the target and second child is the value, so getAssignedValue would check if the node is the ASSIGN's first child and return its next sibling as the value.

Now I'm sketching out a plan for the concrete test suite, aiming for solid coverage without going overboard—maybe 60-90 test methods or grouped assertions given how large the class is.

I'll organize tests by method groups and set up a helper class with private builder methods for constructing nodes, while checking that I have the right Token constants available for the various node types I'll need.

GET and SET seem to be used directly in the source, so that's fine. Now I'm planning the test structure by category: first testing getExpressionBooleanValue with ASSIGN, COMMA, NOT, AND, OR, HOOK cases, then moving into another test group.

For getBooleanValue, I need to cover STRING empty/nonempty, NUMBER zero/nonzero, NULL, FALSE, VOID, NAME variants like undefined/NaN/Infinity/other, TRUE, ARRAYLIT, OBJECTLIT, REGEXP, and default cases returning UNKNOWN. Then getStringValue needs STRING, NAME variants, NUMBER integer/fraction, TRUE/FALSE/NULL, VOID, and default null cases; getNumberValue mirrors similar logic with TRUE/FALSE/NULL/NUMBER/VOID/NAME variants defaulting to null; and getFunctionName requires checking parent NAME, parent ASSIGN, and default cases with and without a name, which means I need to construct function nodes and pull the name from the first child.

I'm continuing through the remaining test cases: getNearestFunctionName's named vs unnamed and parent STRING checks, isImmutableValue covering STRING/NUMBER/NULL/TRUE/FALSE as true with VOID/NEG recursion and NAME variants, isLiteralValue for ARRAYLIT/OBJECTLIT/FUNCTION combinations, isValidDefineValue's binary/unary operator and qualified name checks, isEmptyBlock's various BLOCK configurations, isSimpleOperator's true/false cases, and finally precedence testing where I need to figure out which token type triggers the default error case.

Continuing with associativity, commutativity, and assignment operator checks, then moving into containsFunction/referencesThis tests where I'm constructing trees with THIS nested inside FUNCTION versus placed directly, followed by getAssignedValue tests covering NAME nodes under VAR versus ASSIGN parents and the edge case where the NAME isn't the first child of an ASSIGN.

I'm also planning coverage for isForIn (checking FOR node child counts), isLoopStructure across FOR/DO/WHILE, getLoopCodeBlock's differing child-position logic per loop type, and isControlStructure/isControlStructureCodeBlock exercising each branch like FOR/WHILE/LABEL/WITH, DO, IF, TRY/CATCH, SWITCH/CASE/DEFAULT, and the default fallback case using LABEL.

Reviewing the switch cases, I realize every control structure type is already explicitly handled, so the default branch is effectively unreachable in practice -- I'll skip testing it further and move to getConditionExpression, checking IF/WHILE's first child, DO's last child, and FOR's null case when it has three children.

Then I run through the remaining checks: isStatementBlock for SCRIPT/BLOCK, isStatement based on parent type, isSwitchCase for CASE/DEFAULT, isReferenceName for non-empty NAME nodes, isLabelName, isTryFinallyNode requiring three children with the last matching, and finally removeChild across various parent types.

I'm covering the different parent scenarios for removeChild (BLOCK, SWITCH, TRY, VAR with single/multiple children cascading, LABEL, FOR with four children replaced by EMPTY, else throwing), followed by tryMergeBlock behavior depending on whether the parent is a statement block, plus checks for calls, functions, function bodies, this-references, and function declaration variants.

Now I'm going through more helper predicates: object call methods (call/apply detection), isLhs, object literal key checks, opToStr and opToStrNoFail behavior for known versus unknown tokens, containsType, getVarsDeclaredInBranch, prototype property declaration helpers, node constructors for undefined and var nodes, and finally isLatin/isValidPropertyName testing valid identifiers versus reserved keywords like "if" or "var".

I'm continuing through the list — checking reference counting functions (getNodeTypeReferenceCount, isNameReferenced), visitor traversal helpers tested via custom counting visitors, finally-block and catch-handler detection, function parameter extraction, constant naming checks, and noting that isConstantByConvention and JSDoc-related functions like getFunctionInfo depend on external types (CodingConvention, JSDocInfo) that may need careful handling or skipping.

Then I map out the many branches in evaluatesToLocalValue — assignment, comma, logical operators, hooks, increment/decrement with property flags, this-references, name immutability, property access, function calls (including side-effect flags and toString detection), constructors, literals, and the fallback case that throws an IllegalStateException for unhandled tokens like THROW, which I want to specifically test.

Next I want to cover the argument-extraction helpers and the private toString-call check indirectly through the CALL branch, then move to mayHaveSideEffects and its helper — testing numbers as side-effect-free, throw statements as effectful, object/array/regex literals depending on whether new-object checks are enabled, variable declarations with and without initializers, function expressions versus declarations, constructors with and without side effects, calls with and without side effects, and assignment targets that should register as having side effects.

I'll keep this to a reasonable subset rather than exhaustive coverage, then move into constructorCallHasSideEffects (throwing if not a NEW node, returning false for no-side-effect calls or known constructors, true otherwise), functionCallHasSideEffects (checking no-side-effect calls, built-in names, toString/valueOf-style method calls, Math namespace calls, and defaulting to true), nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects (true for assignment/delete/increment/throw, delegating for calls and news, checking children for names), and canBeSideEffected (true for calls, news, non-constant names, property/element access, false for function expressions, recursing otherwise).

For callHasLocalResult, I'm skipping it since setting side-effect flags on nodes requires uncertain API methods I'm not confident exist, and I want to avoid guessing. I'm deciding to focus the test suite on clear, verifiable branches rather than fully exhaustive coverage, flagging areas skipped due to uncertain APIs, and double-checking that the Node methods I plan to use (getType, getFirstChild, getLastChild, getNext, getString, getDouble) are ones I've actually seen used in the source.

Checking Node constructor overloads...

Actually I found confirmation that Node(int type) alone also exists, seen in removeChild's usage of a placeholder EMPTY node. So both constructors are available, and now I'll move on to writing helper methods for building compound nodes.

I also want to check whether Node.tokenToName is accessible outside its package, but since I don't know the exact expected strings it returns, I probably shouldn't rely on it directly in the test anyway.

Also I should verify TernaryValue's API surface—forBoolean, TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN, plus not/and/or/equals—since it's used directly in source and can be trusted as-is.

I want to check the constructor and function side-effect whitelists, like which built-ins ("Array", "Date", "Error", etc.) are flagged as side-effect free, and confirm behavior with test cases like "Array" vs "Foo". For isNoSideEffectsCall() and isOnlyModifiesThisCall(), I'm unsure how these internal flags get set since I don't see obvious setter methods.

Since I can't easily set those flags to true, I'll assume the default is false for a freshly constructed Node and build test scenarios around that assumption, adding a comment noting I can't test the true branch directly. Now I'm moving on to writing the actual test code, starting with getFunctionName which extracts the function's name from its first child node.

Building the function node structure...

I'm simplifying the test by using a simple NAME node "obj" as the assignment target instead of constructing a full GETPROP structure, trusting Node's qualified name computation.

For the default case with a plain function declaration, I need the function name node to hold a non-empty string like "myFunc" and the parent to not be NAME or ASSIGN.

I'm setting up a test where the function's name resolves to "myFunc" via the default case since the length isn't zero, then testing another case where an empty name should return null.

For the nearest-function-name lookup, I'm constructing a scenario where the function is anonymous but sits inside an object literal as the value of a string key, so the lookup should trace up through the STRING-typed parent to find that key's name.

I'm also verifying the case where the parent isn't a STRING node and the function name is null, which should just yield null overall. Then moving to checking that getFunctionBody correctly extracts the last child as the body node.

For isVarArgsFunction, I'm constructing a test where the function body contains a NAME node for "arguments" so that isNameReferenced picks it up regardless of the surrounding context.

Given the scope of this file, I'm deciding to skip a few methods that depend on CodingConvention or exact flag internals -- like isConstantByConvention, the newQualifiedNameNode/newName variants, and the precise callHasLocalResult flag setting -- and I'll comment those as intentionally skipped rather than testing everything exhaustively.

For getFunctionInfo/getInfoForNameNode, JSDocInfo instances aren't easily constructed here, so I'll just cover the trivial branch where no JSDocInfo is present at all, and accept that this test class won't be perfectly exhaustive while still being well-organized and reasonably thorough.

I'm double-checking that the Node constants I'm relying on—LABEL_NAME, GET, SET, DELPROP, FLAG_LOCAL_RESULTS, IS_CONSTANT_NAME, ORIGINALNAME_PROP, SOURCENAME_PROP—are accessible as public static fields on Node, since I've seen them referenced with the Node prefix elsewhere in the source.

Now I'm sketching helper methods for building nodes: small wrappers for creating name, string, and number nodes, plus a generic node-builder that takes a type and variable children, constructing the first child via the constructor and appending the rest with addChildToBack.

I'll scale back to around 60 focused test methods that group multiple assertions each, keeping solid branch coverage without going overboard. I'm noting the needed imports like TernaryValue for boolean assertions and standard collections utilities for defines sets, then moving to write the final code and summary table.

For the getVarsDeclaredInBranch test, I'm planning a tree with VAR nodes containing NAME children so the visitor collects unique names, verifying duplicates only count once and that nested function scopes get excluded since the traversal predicate stops recursion into FUNCTION nodes' children.

Building the test tree with duplicate "a" declarations plus a nested function containing its own var...

I'm asserting that the collector returns only two vars ("a" and "b"), confirming duplicates aren't double-counted and the inner function's variable is excluded—good coverage for the visitor logic.

Now I'm writing a helper that constructs a function node with a given name and body, setting up empty parameters and attaching the body block. Next I want to test whether a function node is treated as a declaration versus an expression depending on its parent context, like a block versus an assignment.

I need it to check that the parent is SCRIPT, or that the grandparent is FUNCTION. Testing case A, where the function's parent is a SCRIPT node directly, that satisfies isStatement and should make isHoistedFunctionDeclaration return true through the first condition. Now I'm setting up case B, checking a function nested inside another function's body.

I realize the second condition would call getType() on a null parent, causing an NPE, so I need to wrap the block in a non-function parent to avoid that crash while still testing the "not hoisted" case correctly.

Now I'm turning to isEmptyFunctionExpression, which checks that a node is a function expression with an empty block body. I'll build test cases with an empty-body expression function (should be true), a non-empty body (false), and a function declaration instead of expression (also false regardless of body).

With the logic mapped out, I'll write the full test file, covering exception cases like precedence on unknown types throwing Error, invalid assignment ops throwing IllegalArgumentException, and side-effect checks on non-NEW nodes throwing IllegalStateException.

I need to make sure removeChild test cases are constructed carefully, building proper parent-child node structures like BLOCK containing EXPR_RESULT to verify statement removal behaves correctly.

For the switch case scenario, I'm noting that isSwitchCase checks the node itself (CASE/DEFAULT), not the parent, so building a SWITCH node with a CASE child and calling removeChild should exercise the generic parent.removeChild path regardless of parent type.

Now I'm thinking through the try-finally node removal case as another distinct branch to test.

Beyond that, I want to verify VAR node removal with multiple children versus a single child - the multi-child case should just remove one NAME leaving the rest, while the single-child case triggers recursive removal since VAR itself becomes empty and its parent block needs cleanup too.

For BLOCK-type nodes, I'm testing that regardless of the parent's type, removeChild falls through to the detachChildren branch since node.getType()==BLOCK is checked directly - I'll build a simple IF node containing a condition and a BLOCK child, call removeChild, and confirm the block's children are all detached afterward.

Next I need to cover LABEL nodes: when node is the last child of a LABEL (the statement, not the label name), removeChild first strips it from the LABEL, then recursively removes the LABEL itself from its own parent - this should work cleanly if that parent is a BLOCK or SCRIPT.

Then I need a case for FOR loops with 4 children (init, cond, incr, body vs the 3-child for-in form), where removing a middle piece like the condition should trigger a replaceChild swap instead of a plain removal.

Finally, for the default else branch throwing IllegalStateException, I want a parent/node combo that doesn't match any of the recognized structural patterns, so I can confirm that invalid case fails as expected.

That should cover removeChild well enough — time to finalize the test file. Next I'll design tryMergeBlock tests: merging a nested BLOCK into its parent BLOCK should succeed and remove the child, while calling it on a block whose parent isn't a BLOCK (like an IF) should return false and leave the tree untouched.

For the finally/catch helpers, I need TRY nodes with two children (no finally) versus three (has finally), and I'm working out how getCatchBlock and hasCatchHandler navigate the TRY node's catch-container child to detect an actual CATCH node inside it.

I'm checking hasFinally logic with two vs three children, then verifying getFnParameters returns the LP node from a manually built function, and confirming isConstantName reads the IS_CONSTANT_NAME boolean prop correctly before moving to getSourceName's property lookup.

For getSourceName, I'm building a parent-child chain where only the grandparent has the SOURCENAME_PROP set, testing that the lookup climbs ancestors to find it, and also confirming it returns null when no ancestor has the prop. Then I move to verifying newCallNode constructs a proper CALL node with the target name as first child and the correct argument children.

I'm also checking that FREE_CALL is set true when the call target is a plain name node, and false when the target is something like a property access. Finally I test newVarNode, confirming it produces a VAR node wrapping a NAME child that holds the given identifier and value, and that passing null for the value results in no child under the NAME node.

For newUndefinedNode, I verify it produces a VOID node whose child is a NUMBER literal with value zero, and that passing a source reference node doesn't throw when copying position info. Then I build a FUNCTION node with newFunctionNode, checking the name, parameter list, and body block are structured correctly, and use that setup to test that getArgumentForFunction correctly retrieves parameters by index or returns null when out of range.

Now I move to testing getArgumentForCallOrNew similarly, then start on evaluatesToLocalValue: for ASSIGN nodes, I confirm that if the right-hand side is immutable (like a number literal), the result is true regardless of the locals predicate, since immutability is checked first via OR logic. I also test the case where the right-hand side isn't immutable and the locals predicate always returns false, expecting both conditions to fail.

For COMMA nodes, I check that evaluatesToLocalValue looks at the last child—testing with a trailing string literal, which is immutable, so the recursive check returns true. For AND/OR nodes, I test with both operands as immutable numbers, expecting the recursive conjunction to evaluate to true.

I also want to test AND with one non-immutable branch (a plain NAME reference) to confirm it returns false. For HOOK nodes, I need to verify the structure has three children—condition, true branch, false branch—and test cases where both branches are immutable (true) versus where one branch is a non-immutable NAME (false). Now I'm setting up an INC/DEC test node wrapping a NAME target.

For THIS, using an always-true predicate for locals should give a true result. For NAME, an immutable name like Infinity returns true regardless of locals, while a non-immutable name depends on whether locals is always-true or always-false. Now I'm considering GETELEM/GETPROP cases with the same locals predicate logic.

For CALL, since I don't have a setter API for side-effect flags, callHasLocalResult likely defaults to false unless flags are set. I'm also checking isToStringMethodCall by building a call node where the target is a GETPROP for obj.toString, which should evaluate to true for toString method calls even without local results.

For NEW, FUNCTION, REGEXP, ARRAYLIT, and OBJECTLIT, these all return true unconditionally regardless of side-effect flags, so I'm testing each by constructing the respective node type and confirming evaluatesToLocalValue returns true.

For IN, it also returns true unconditionally per the source, so testing an IN node with two names confirms that. For the default fallback path, isAssignmentOp, isSimpleOperator, or isImmutableValue determine the result—testing ADD as a simple operator should return true, while checking something unclassified like THROW might trigger the IllegalStateException branch, though I need to consider whether THROW is even reachable as a value expression in practice.

I'm confirming that THROW falls outside all the recognized categories, so a node like n(Token.THROW, num(1)) should throw IllegalStateException as expected—and I've verified that calling value.getParent() inside the error message won't cause an NPE since Java string concatenation safely converts null to "null" text.

Now I'm planning tests for constructorCallHasSideEffects: a non-NEW node should throw IllegalStateException, while a NEW node wrapping a NAME like "Array" (which is in the whitelist of side-effect-free constructors) should return false, assuming side-effect flags default to false.

For unknown NEW targets, like "Foo", the result should be true, and for a NEW node whose target isn't even a NAME (like a GETPROP), it should still fall through to true since the whitelist check only applies to NAME nodes.

I'm also mapping out functionCallHasSideEffects: a non-CALL node throws, a CALL to a builtin like "Object" returns false, an unknown function call defaults to true, and a CALL through a GETPROP ending in "toString" with no arguments needs its own case since it's checking whether the call has exactly one child.

For GETPROP calls, I need cases where the method isn't in the known side-effect-free list (falls to true), and where the receiver is the "Math" namespace, which should always return false regardless of the method name. I'm noting that the isOnlyModifiesThisCall and compiler-dependent REGEXP/STRING branches can be skipped since there's no setter API and compiler is null, bypassing those inner checks entirely.

Now moving to nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects: assignment ops return true immediately, and DELPROP/DEC/INC/THROW each individually return true. CALL and NEW delegate to their respective side-effect checks (builtin Math calls and Array constructors return false, unknown ones return true), NAME nodes with an initializer child return true while bare NAME nodes return false, and I'm working through the remaining default cases.

For canBeSideEffected: CALL/NEW always return true, NAME depends on whether it's a constant or in the known-constants set, and GETPROP/GETELEM always return true. For FUNCTION nodes there's a precondition that it must be an expression, so I need to test that a declaration throws an exception while a proper function expression returns false. The default case recurses into children, so a BLOCK with only a STRING returns false while one containing a CALL returns true since the recursion finds it.

Now I'm starting on mayHaveSideEffects and the state-change helper, testing that a plain NUMBER node yields false.

I'm noting THROW nodes always return true immediately. For OBJECTLIT, when checkForNewObjects is true it returns true right away, but when false it depends on whether the values inside are side-effect-free — string key/value pairs stay false, but a CALL to an unknown function inside makes it true. I'm working out the tree structure where each key node holds its value as a child, then moving on to ARRAYLIT and REGEXP cases.

Continuing through the logic: ARRAYLIT with checkForNewObjects true returns true, otherwise it checks children — plain numbers keep it false while a side-effecting CALL flips it to true. I'm also tracing VAR/NAME nodes (an initializer makes it true, no child means false) and the FUNCTION case, where function expressions evaluate to false but function declarations evaluate to true under the same formula, before moving into NEW node handling.

For NEW nodes, checkForNewObjects true returns true immediately; otherwise I check whether the constructor call is known safe (like "Array") versus unknown, which forces true. Similarly for CALL nodes, known side-effect-free functions like Math calls fall through to check their arguments, while unknown functions default to true. I'm also working through the default case for simple operators and assignment expressions — assigning to a NAME is always a side effect, while assigning to a GETPROP depends on whether the base object evaluates to a local value.

So with "new Array()" replacing the ctor, GETPROP now evaluates to false overall since both the NEW and STRING children are side-effect free, and the RHS NUMBER is also false, satisfying both preconditions. Now I move to the isGet branch: getting the first child of assignTarget (the NEW node) and checking whether it evaluates to a local value.

Since NEW always returns true per the switch statement, this path returns false directly, meaning no side effect. I'm now testing the other branch where evaluatesToLocalValue returns false — using a plain NAME node like "obj" as the base of a GETPROP. Since NAME isn't immutable and the default locals function returns false, it doesn't evaluate to a local value, so I unwrap through the loop and check isLiteralValue on the NAME, which should be false, meaning the side-effect flag should end up true for this case.

I'm also verifying that the assignment target's children (the property STRING and the RHS number literal) contribute no additional side effects, then moving to the fallback branch where the assign target isn't a NAME or GET expression at all — testing what happens with a stranger target like a numeric literal used as an assignment target to see if it falls through to the literal-value check correctly.

With that edge case handled, I feel this covers the branch coverage well enough for the isAssignmentOp logic, so I'll move on to actually finalizing and writing out the test code despite its length.

Adding imports and test class setup...

Adding a helper to construct function nodes, then planning to write out all the test methods grouped by comments.
